title: Obedience
definition: Obedience is the faithful response of trusting God and doing what He commands in Scripture.
summary: Obedience is the fruit of faith and love for God, not the attempt to earn salvation.
christFocus: Jesus perfectly obeyed the Father and calls His disciples to follow Him in loving obedience.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Obedience flows from faith. It is not a way to purchase salvation, but the proper response of those who have been saved by grace. God speaks, and His people are called to trust and obey.

Biblical obedience is not selective submission. It involves hearing the Word, receiving it with humility, and practicing it in daily life. It touches speech, relationships, forgiveness, holiness, worship, work, stewardship, and mission.

Obedience is also Christ-centered. Jesus obeyed perfectly where sinners have failed, and by His grace believers are renewed to walk in His ways.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people want comfort from Scripture without submission to Scripture. Obedience matters because discipleship is not merely knowing what Jesus said; it is following Him.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Identify one area where God's Word is calling for action. Do not delay obedience because it is costly. Trust Christ, ask for help, and take the next faithful step.
